subject.title: fix(zalo): journal polled updates before dispatch

question: Should Zalo polling intentionally change from globally serial dispatch to the shared ingress drain’s concurrent cross-chat delivery model while retaining per-chat lane ordering?
rationale: The durability repair is well-supported, but the central code change also changes delivery scheduling semantics that existing polling users may observe under concurrent chats or failures.

options.title: Accept shared ingress concurrency
options.body: Merge with the queue’s existing concurrent delivery behavior, relying on per-chat lanes to preserve conversation ordering.

options.title: Preserve polling backpressure
options.body: Adjust the polling integration so durable admission remains in place while polling retains the previous globally serial dispatch behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept shared ingress concurrency
recommendation.body: Merge with the queue’s existing concurrent delivery behavior, relying on per-chat lanes to preserve conversation ordering.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the shared Zalo ingress contract and are best placed to decide whether polling should inherit its delivery scheduling behavior.
